title: Identifying Feedback-Cycle Polarity in Bivariate Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Models from Stationary Covariance
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 6.1 < ceiling_for_field 7.4; not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The note proves global product-sign nonidentification in the unrestricted bivariate class and an exact finite certificate under imposed edge-margin and norm restrictions, but the unrestricted result is an elementary two-dimensional fiber consequence and the positive identification result remains tied to a narrowly bounded refinement.

The inference converse is established only around one constructed asymmetric zero-diffusion contact, so the advertised frontier is not a general characterization of the certificate boundaries, although the prose eventually discloses this local scope.

No theorem-level claim is left conjectural or proved only one-sidedly, but the practical meaning and calibration of the analyst-chosen eta and M restrictions are unsupported by an application or sensitivity analysis.

The positioning omits relevance/comparison sentences for cited VarandoHansen2020, AmendolaBoegeHolleringMisra2025, and BoegeBoegeHolleringMisra2025; add their precise relation to the unrestricted two-cycle polarity theorem and distinguish their scope from this product-sign result.
proof_attempt_summary: The derivation proved the unrestricted published-class result P_pub(Sigma)={-1,+1}, a complete bounded-margin four-sector certificate with at most eleven active-set candidates, a t-faithful joint-only open region, the asymmetric contact, honest covariance inversion, and matched local root-n recovery and impossibility results. The mathematical review passed without findings, but the general referee graded the package incremental because the unrestricted result is elementary, the positive results remain bivariate and depend on uncalibrated eta/M restrictions, and the inference boundary theory covers only one constructed contact. A field-tier continuation would require a separate all-regular-boundary semialgebraic and LAN program; the bank also preserves the unresolved related-work positioning omission rather than claiming every D0.5 finding was discharged.
tldr: In the unrestricted published bivariate complete-two-cycle SCM, every \(t\)-faithful stationary covariance admits full-support Hurwitz generators of both cycle-product polarities, so Gaussian equilibrium snapshots never identify that product sign. The analyst-imposed refinement instead bounds the scale-invariant raw ratios \(|B_{12}|/\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)\), \(|B_{21}|/\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)\), and \(\lVert B\rVert_F/\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)\), represented after the trace-one gauge by \(\eta\) and \(M\). On that refinement, a complete four-sector certificate characterizes the compatible polarity set, including every strict-diffusion and norm-attainment branch, equal-variance thresholds, an asymmetric contact, honest covariance-region inversion, uniform singleton recovery beyond root-\(n\) clearance, and a matching local Gaussian obstruction.
gap: Van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar characterize signs one drift edge at a time and explicitly leave subgraph and graph-level signs open. Dettling, Homs, Améndola, Drton, and Hansen identify the directed two-cycle as the obstruction to full drift recovery under fixed diagonal volatility, but do not characterize a coarser sign quotient along its affine Lyapunov fiber. Neither result resolves strict-diffusion attainment or sampling uncertainty at the resulting contact sets.
fill: The project first records the common time-scale equivalence and its unique trace-one representative, then derives an exact finite semialgebraic certificate for the compatible loop-polarity set, proves its open-versus-closed branches, gives closed-form equal-variance and asymmetric-contact reductions, and propagates the population set through a Gaussian covariance confidence region with local sharpness at regular contacts.
